statement: In every declared system, each member's runs_on resolves to another member that is present in the system.
rationale: A system that names a dependency it does not contain is describing something other than itself. This is the cheapest integrity check the architecture layer can run and it is the one that catches a declared assembly being a wish list. It deliberately does not check that the resolved member is LOWER in the stack: no document in this repository declares a total order over the layer roles, and inventing one to make the test stricter would settle by fiat a question nobody has answered. The gap is printed on every run.
prediction: Across all systems under systems/, zero runs_on targets fail to resolve to a present member, zero members name an entry that does not exist, and zero members carry a role or runs_on declaration that conflicts with the entry's own.

measures.target: whether the declared assemblies hold together as assemblies
measures.rendering: resolving runs_on targets against system membership
measures.target_question: Does a system whose runs_on all resolve actually hold together, or does resolution only show that the declarations are internally consistent?

last_result.summary: every runs_on target in 1 evaluable system(s) resolves to a present member
